title: Stand Atlantic Bag First ARIA No. 1 With ‘GODBREATH’
summary: The Sydneysiders becomes the fourth Australian rock act to lead the national chart in 2026.
contentText:
Stand Atlantic is standing tall on the ARIA Chart with GODBREATH (via Virgin Music Group/Inertia), for their first No. 1 on Australia’s national albums tally.

The best-seller for the week on vinyl, GODBREATH is the Sydney rock act’s fourth top 30 appearance on the ARIA Albums Chart following Pink Elephant (No. 23 in 2020), F.E.A.R. (No. 10 in 2022) and Was Here (No. 3 in 2024).

“Only gone n bloody done it.. GODBREATH is the No. 1 Album in Australia!!,” reads a statement from the band. “Thank u for supporting us and Australian music!! Happy GODBREATH week to u all this is cool af and only possible bc of all of u, thank u thank u thank u.”

Led by Bonnie Fraser (vocals and guitar), the band recently completed a string of U.K. dates with Simple Plan, they’re back home for Australian dates before returning to the United States for Vans Warped Tour Orlando and a tour with Story of the Year and Silverstein.

GODBREATH is the fourth homegrown album to lead the chart in 2026, after sets by Karnivool, DMA’s and Angus & Julia Stone. And it’s one of three ARIA top 10 debutants on the new chart, published Friday, Oct. 30.

Also making his mark is Dan Sultan, whose Little Miracles (Mushroom Music) bows at No. 5. A five-time ARIA Award winner, Sultan now has five top 50 results including three top 10s (2014’s Blackbird peaked at No. 4 and 2017’s Killer went to No. 5).

Boo Seeka, the electropop project of Sydney artist Ben “Boo” Gumbleton, lights up for an ARIA top 10 appearance with his independently-released Cigarettes On Sundown , new at No. 10. His debut album Never Too Soon reached No. 8 in 2017.

The latest tally welcomes new releases from Black Sabbath founder Tony Iommi ( From The Dark at No. 16 via BMG/Universal), Melbourne band Surprise Chef ( Frog In A Pond at No. 17 via Concord/Universal), Nashville-based Australian country artist Melanie Dyer ( Daisies From Dirt at No. 23 via ABC/Orchard), Sydney indie rock group The Buoys ( Concrete Cowboy at No. 31 via Sony) and Wagga Wagga, NSW metalcore band Windwaker ( Smile, You’re On Camera at No. 38 via Orchard).

Meanwhile, BLACKPINK’s Lisa lands at No. 34 with Press Play (RCA/Sony), her first solo EP. With that effort, the Thai singer and rapper becomes the third-member of the superstar K-pop group to crack the top 50 with a solo project. Rosé did it first with her self-titled set from 2024, which peaked at No. 2 in 2024, while Jennie also went to No. 2 with 2025’s Ruby . BLACKPINK’s two studio albums, The Album (from 2021) and Born Pink (2022) also peaked at No. 2.

Over on the ARIA Singles Chart , Tate McRae’s “Housewife” (RCA/Sony) logs a second straight week at No. 1.

And finally, Welsh singer Jamie Miller enjoys his first top 10 hit as “Babydoll” (Universal) improves 27-9. Miller became the first Welsh singer to top the Official U.K. Singles Chart in 15 years when “Babydoll” went to the summit there last week.
